$doc: Vyomi capability registry — Azure Log Analytics (Microsoft.OperationalInsights). See servicebus.json for the contract. 'nano' = Nano/dev_server (core/azure_arm_core.py generic catalog + core/azure_operationalinsights_core.py); 'offline' = the appliance, which shares the same generic ARM catalog.

azure.loganalytics.workspace.crud.title: Workspaces — create, list, get, update, delete, pricing tier, retention, daily cap

azure.loganalytics.workspace.agents.title: Agents management — workspace ID and primary/secondary shared keys (getSharedKeys / regenerateSharedKey)
limitations: Keys are simulated values derived from the workspace id, not cryptographically meaningful; no real agent ever authenticates with them.

azure.loganalytics.workspace.usage.title: Usage and estimated costs (usages action) and the daily cap (workspaceCapping)
limitations: Data Analyzed always reads 0 bytes — there is no ingestion pipeline to meter; Tables and Saved searches counts are real.

azure.loganalytics.workspace.savedsearch.title: Saved searches — create, list, get, update, delete

azure.loganalytics.workspace.tables.title: Tables — built-in tables plus custom (_CL/_RST) table create/update/delete, retention and plan

azure.loganalytics.workspace.datasources.title: Data sources — create, list (by kind), get, delete
limitations: Data sources are stored and listed like real ARM but never receive data — there is no VM extension/agent in this simulator to collect from.

azure.loganalytics.workspace.legacysolut.title: Legacy solutions (intelligencePacks) — list, enable, disable
limitations: Enabling a solution only flips its flag; it does not add the solution's own tables or saved searches.

azure.loganalytics.workspace.logs.title: Logs — KQL query editor (api/query), a real subset of KQL over real data
limitations: Only a small KQL subset is understood: a table name, then where (==/!=/contains/startswith), project, sort by/order by, take/limit and count — summarize, join and the rest of the language raise the real ARM-shaped error rather than a silent empty result.

The AzureActivity table returns real rows (this subscription's Activity log feed); every other built-in table (Heartbeat, Perf, Syslog, Event, Usage, AzureDiagnostics) and every custom table is always empty — there is no agent/telemetry ingestion pipeline to populate them.
The api.loganalytics.io data-plane host (azure-monitor-query / LogsQueryClient) is not modelled — only the ARM pass-through path the portal's Logs blade itself uses.

azure.loganalytics.workspace.locks.title: Resource locks (Microsoft.Authorization/locks), scoped to this workspace
limitations: Enforcement is not modelled for this resource type — a lock is stored and listed like real ARM but does not block a write or delete on the workspace.

Locks are only simulated at the resource scope (this workspace); subscription- and resource-group-scoped lock lists are an honest 'Not simulated' gap, same as the real Subscription/Resource group scope-switch buttons.

azure.loganalytics.workspace.activitylog.title: Workspace activity log
limitations: Only console/SDK-triggered mutations made since the simulation booted are recorded (no historical backfill); severity/category filtering and the 7/30/90-day timespan picker are not modelled, and `caller` is a fixed placeholder identity rather than the real signed-in principal.

azure.loganalytics.workspace.listactions.title: Toolbar actions needing a separate Azure product or a per-row detail flyout: Activity log's Export Activity Logs, and Locks' Subscription/Resource group scope + Feedback
limitations: Continuous Export Activity Logs (to Storage/Event Hub/Log Analytics), the per-event Activity detail flyout, and portal Feedback are not modeled.

Column customization, one-time CSV export, filtering and 'Reset to default' on both the Activity log and Locks panels ARE real (consoles/src/azure/kit/BrowseGrid.jsx, client-side over the real rows) — this entry covers only the actions listed above.

azure.loganalytics.workspace.exporttempl.title: Export template (ARM template)
limitations: Only the ARM Template tab is generated from the workspace's real properties; Bicep and Terraform export are not modeled.

azure.loganalytics.workspace.iam.title: Access control (IAM) on a workspace
limitations: Check access, Role assignments and Deny assignments are REAL and scoped to this workspace's resource id: Check access runs core/azure_iam_core.py's evaluator (explicit-deny-wins, scope inheritance from the subscription/resource group), the lists filter the shared RBAC store to assignments whose scope covers it, and new assignments are created scoped to it. Principal IDs are free text (Vyomi has no real directory); 'My access' and Classic administrators stay honest gaps.

azure.loganalytics.workspace.networking.title: Public network access for ingestion/query (set at create time and from Properties)
limitations: Vyomi stores publicNetworkAccessForIngestion/Query exactly as configured and returns it from the API, but never actually blocks a query or data-source write based on it.

azure.loganalytics.workspace.monitoring.title: Alerts, Metrics, Diagnostic settings and Workbooks on a workspace
limitations: Metrics charts, alert rules, diagnostic-setting log routing and Workbooks are not modeled.

azure.loganalytics.workspace.tools.title: Diagnose and solve problems, Computer groups (classic), Data export, Linked storage accounts, Resource health, and Support + Troubleshooting
limitations: These portal troubleshooting, agent-based computer grouping, continuous data export and linked-storage-account features are not modeled.
